why: Track the furthest reach so far: a part that starts here must extend at least to the last occurrence of every letter it contains. Scan, keep end = max(last[c]); when the index reaches end, cut.
hints: If a part contains letter c, how far right must that part extend at minimum?

Precompute last[c] for each letter. While scanning, the current part's end is the furthest last occurrence among its letters; it can only grow. When i == end, nothing inside reaches further, so cutting here is safe and as early as possible.
last = {c: i}; walk i with end = max(end, last[text[i]]); when i == end append end - start + 1 and set start = i + 1. O(n).
pitfalls: Empty text returns an empty list.
Cutting as soon as i == end is what makes the number of parts maximal; do not wait for the letter to change.
